docs.title: Introduktion
docs.text:
Maya1 er et open-source værktøj til at lave hjemmesider, der kan søge i og vise materialer fra Aarhus Stadsarkivs omfattende samlinger.

Tanken bag Maya er, at det skal være nemt for organisationer, virksomheder og lignende, at oprette deres eget online arkiv, hvor kun materialer med relevans for netop deres institution kan blive fremsøgt og vist. Eneste forudsætning er, at materialerne er registreret som en del af Aarhus Stadsarkivs samlinger :)

Sallingarkivet.dk er første eksempel på en hjemmeside, der er bygget på Maya, men flere er på vej...

Vi har også publiceret en demo-side, som viser, hvordan en rå Maya-baseret hjemmeside ser ud, før man har konfigureret både det visuelle udtryk, indholdet og funktionaliteten.

Maya er udviklet af Aarhus Stadsarkiv, men kildekoden er open source og offentlig tilgængelig på Github, og har man lyst, er man velkommen til at bidrage.

Slutteligt en stor tak til Sallingfondene, der har støttet projektet økonomisk!

  1. Maya er en forkortelse for My Archive, Your Archive. Det var det bedste vi kunne finde på, og så var der mulighed for et cool logo! ↩

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
For at teste, udvikle og efterfølgende sætte en Maya-baseret web-klient i produktion, skal man bruge en API-nøgle.

API-nøglen er ikke offentlig, så pas på med at pushe den til Github eller hvilket versionsstyringsprogram man end måtte bruge. For at få udleveret en API-nøgle skal sende en mail til Aarhus Stadsarkiv (stadsarkiv@aarhus.dk) med emnet: "API-nøgle til Maya".

docs.title: .env vs. ENVIRONMENT
docs.text:
Den nemmeste måde at håndtere API-nøglen på, er at gemme den i en .env-fil i roden af projektets BASE_DIR med navnet "API_KEY". Eksempelvis:

me@LAPTOP:~/min-maya-klient$ cat .env
API_KEY=your_api_key

Bemærk

.env-filer er blot simple key-value filer, der bruges til at gemme variabler, ofte af privat karakter: 

SUPER_SECRET_API_KEY = "a;ljskdshhhDONTTELLkljasdfhio"
DATABASE_URL=secrets://username:password@localhost:11/secrets
OTHER_SECRET = "awefWhatevERjlk;a"

Alternativt kan man benytte API-nøglen direkte som en miljøvariabel.

Links til linux, mac og pc

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Maya er primært tænkt som et kommandline værktøj, men hvis man vil, kan man også clone github-repo'et, for ydermere at se, hvordan det er bygget og eventuelt bidrage til udviklingen af værktøjet.

Det er muligt at installere Maya på alle platforme, der har pipx eller uv installeret.

docs.title: Brug pipx
docs.text:
pipx er et program til at installere python-baseret software inklusiv alle dets afhængigheder i isolerede miljøer, hvorved man undgår at installere programmer direkte i ens styresystem. Hvis du har pipx på dit system, installerer du maya således:

$ pipx install git+https://github.com/aarhusstadsarkiv/maya.git

docs.title: Brug uv
docs.text:
uv er et package- og projektmanagement program til håndtering af python applikationer, men det indholder også et pipx-ækvivalent værktøj, hvormed du kan installere maya:

$ uv tool install git+https://github.com/aarhusstadsarkiv/maya.git

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
Maya udstiller en række hooks i sin kildekode, der kan bruges til an ændre måden Maya eksekverer sin kode på.

Ved at implementere en eller flere af disse hooks kan man med andre ord skrive en slags letvægtsplugin. Man skal blot bruge @hookimpl decoratoren på en funktion, der er navngivet efter en af Mayas hooks, og som accepterer en eller flere af de dokumenterede parametre, der bliver sendt til det hook.

Alle hook-implementeringer, der er implementeret i et python-modul (.py-fil) i roden af "hooks"-mappen i projektets BASE_DIR, bliver automatisk integereret i Mayas kodeeksekvering. Hvis samme hook er implementeret i flere python-moduler, eksekveres de i alfabetisk rækkefølge.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Maya indeholder en lang række settings, som man kan overskrive efter behov.

En setting findes i enten settings.yml, facets.yml eller language.yml (oplistet nedenfor), og hvis man vil overskrive en setting, skal man oprette en tilsvarende yaml-fil i roden af BASE_DIR. Hvis man eksempelvis vil ændre om Maya gemmer på seneste søgning mens man navigerer rundt på andre sider, sætter man værdien til false:

# settings.yml
search_keep_results: false

docs.title: Search browser challenge
docs.text:
search_challenge_enabled defaults to true. Before /search runs any API calls, visitors complete an automatic JavaScript proof of work and a minimum two-second wait, then select Continue to search. The button becomes available only when both checks are complete; there is no automatic redirect. It supports mouse and keyboard activation. The wait happens in the browser and is checked by the server; no server worker sleeps. Successful verification sets an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie valid for 30 minutes (Secure on HTTPS). Search filters are preserved. The challenge uses Danish when the browser's preferred language (from Accept-Language, including quality weights) is da or a Danish regional variant such as da-DK. All other preferences, or a missing header, use English. This includes the button, progress messages, and verification-error page, with no additional translation or API requests. Both the challenge and verification cookie are bound to the visitor's IP using a keyed hash, without storing the raw IP in either token. Changing IP requires a new challenge. Cookies can still be shared by clients using the same public IP. Deploying the IP-bound version invalidates older challenge and verification tokens; login/session cookies are unaffected.

Serve the site over HTTPS and keep SESSION_SECRET persistent and identical across workers. The challenge expires after five minutes. Visitors need JavaScript and cookies. /search/json returns HTTP 403 with search_verification_required until the browser has completed /search. Other endpoints, including record pages and autocomplete, are unchanged. Challenge and verified search responses must not be cached by a shared proxy.

IP binding uses the ASGI client address, also shown in Maya's access logs; it does not read forwarded headers directly. Configure Gunicorn/Uvicorn's FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS to trust only Caddy's actual connecting address, never * on a publicly reachable server. For Caddy on the same machine, use a loopback upstream and bind Maya with --host 127.0.0.1. If Caddy connects from another machine/container, set the trusted proxy address explicitly and restrict direct access to Gunicorn. Confirm access logs contain actual visitor addresses, not one shared proxy address, before relying on IP binding.

This deters simple crawlers, not determined browser automation. Clearance can be reused for its lifetime and requests still reach Python. Keep concurrency limits and upstream traffic protection. No database or additional service is required. Restart Maya after deploying; no Caddy plugin is needed.

docs.title: Office IP exemptions
docs.text:
search_challenge_allowed_ips defaults to an empty list. List individual public IPv4 or IPv6 addresses to let legacy office clients use /search and its subpaths (including /search/json) without JavaScript or a verification cookie:

search_challenge_allowed_ips:
  - "192.0.2.10"  # Example only; replace with your office's public IP.

Ranges, CIDR notation, and hostnames are not accepted. Everyone sharing a listed public IP is exempt. The same trusted ASGI client address used for IP binding is used here; supplied forwarding headers are not read directly. Concurrency limits, authentication, and authorization still apply. Exempt requests log challenge=allowed reason=allowlisted_ip and do not issue verification cookies. Keep actual office addresses in untracked local settings. For a deployed site using a separate BASE_DIR such as local, add the setting there and restart Maya; upgrading the package alone does not copy site settings.

docs.title: Challenge access logging
docs.text:
The existing access log includes challenge=issued, challenge=passed, challenge=failed, or challenge=allowed on requests handled by the challenge. An optional reason= explains issuance or rejection, for example missing_cookie, expired_cookie, invalid_signature, ip_mismatch, too_early, expired_challenge, or invalid_proof. No additional log entry is written. Tokens, cookies, proof solutions, and IP fingerprints are not added to logs; query strings on /_search-challenge are omitted as well.

issued means only that a challenge page was served. A visitor who never submits it creates no failed event. passed means verification succeeded, not that the visitor is necessarily human. allowed means a valid cookie admitted the request; check its HTTP status and duration for search failures. failed also covers protected JSON requests rejected without a valid cookie; filter to POST /_search-challenge when counting verification failures. Requests rejected by concurrency limits before reaching the challenge retain their ordinary 429 access entry with no challenge outcome.

Browsers usually omit expired cookies, which is logged as missing_cookie; expired_cookie is reported only when an expired cookie is actually submitted. Compare outcome counts over time with search latency, API timeouts, and CPU load. Counts represent requests, not unique people or bots.

To disable the challenge in a site's settings:

search_challenge_enabled: false
